sentences.text:
This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner seeking quashment of FIR bearing crime No.62/2022 registered at Police Station Kotwali District Gwalior against the petitioner for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 of IPC.
2.

As per prosecution case, the complainant/respondent No.4 lodged the impugend FIR stating that the father and uncle of the complainant had purchased 1854 square feet of land situated near Balabai Ki Chhatri, Hanuman Bandh Nala, Nagar Lashkar, Gwalior, from Smt. Suninda Raje Shitole through a registered sale deed dated 01.10.1995.

After purchasing the said property, a written exchange deed between the complainant's father Rajendra Kumar Jain and his uncle Narendra Kumar Jain was executed and registered on 23.03.2009, pursuant to which the entire 1854 square feet of land came into the share of the complainant's father.

Subsequently, in respect of 1070 square feet of the said land, the complainant's father NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 2 MCRC-16712-2022 executed a general power of attorney (Mukhtyarnama Aam) in favour of Hemant Pal on 05.08.2010, authorizing him to sell the said portion of land, which was duly registered in the office of the Sub-Registrar on the same date.
Furthermore, the complainant's father also executed a written agreement before a notary on 17.08.2010 in favour of Hemant Pal concerning the said 1070 square feet of land.
Thereafter, on 14.08.2012, another written agreement was executed between the complainant's father and Hemant Pal regarding the remaining 784 square feet of land.

However,

sentences.text: under the pretext of getting this agreement registered, two days after the execution of the said agreement, i.e., on 16.08.2012, Hemant Pal took the complainant's father to the Registrar's office and, by deceitfully misleading him, fraudulently prepared a forged general power of attorney for 1070 square feet of land instead of 784 square feet, and obtained his signatures on it, despite the fact that only 784 square feet of land remained in the name of the complainant's father at that time.

On the basis of the said forged general power of attorney, Hemant Pal executed a registered sale deed dated 13.08.2013 transferring 860 square feet of land in the name of his maternal uncle Bharat Baghel (present petitioner), son of Badriprasad Baghel, resident of Daulatganj.
The complainant's father Rajendra Kumar Jain passed away on 17.09.2020 due to COVID-19.

After his demise, when the complainant initiated mutation proceedings in the Municipal Corporation in the year 2020, and while the said mutation process was still pending, Geeta, wife of Vidharam Rathore, began dismantling the structure (Pataur) situated on the said land, whereupon the complainant came to know that Hemant Pal had NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 3 MCRC-16712-2022 fraudulently sold the land to Bharat Baghel on the basis of the forged power of attorney dated 13.08.2013, and Bharat Baghel had subsequently sold the same land to Geeta, wife of Vidharam Rathore.

Thus, by deceitfully obtaining the signatures of the complainant's father on a forged general power of attorney instead of the intended agreement document and subsequently selling the land, Hemant Pal and Bharat Baghel have committed fraud and forgery.
On the basis of the aforesaid allegations, the present FIR has been registered against the present petitioner and the co- accused person.

3. The present petition has been filed by the petitioner on the following grounds:-
1. That the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the aforesaid case and no such incident has been caused or committed by him in any manner whatsoever.
The petitioner has neither any direct nor indirect connection with the alleged offence mentioned above.

2. That the petitioner, on 13/08/2013, purchased a plot situated at Ward No. 49,
Hanuman Bandhi, Pargana and District Gwalior, which was under the ownership and title of Shri Rajendra Jain, son of Shri Guljari Lal Jain, resident of Teli Ki Bajariya,
Lashkar, Gwalior.
3. That the said plot had earlier been authorized by Shri Rajendra Kumar Jain in favour of Hemant Pal, son of Omprakash Pal, resident of Tikonia Murar, Gwalior, by appointing him as his lawful representative before the Registrar on 16/08/2012.
Prior to purchasing the said plot measuring 28.6 30.3 square feet, ie, approximately 862.136 square feet, the applicant had duly contacted Rajendra Jain regarding the sale.
Thereafter, a sale agreement was executed by the petitioner for a total consideration of 28,02,000.

The agreement was duly registered in the office of the Registrar, Gwalior, in the presence of witnesses Sanjay Pal, resident of Bakshi Ki Mithi Daulatganj, and Kamal Kishore, resident of Nimbalkar Ki Goth, Lashkar, on 13/08/2013

Subsequently, the applicant also obtained lawful mutation of the said property in his name in the Municipal Corporation, Gwalior, vide order dated Bharat Baghel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73539724/

That after retaining the said plot for approximately nine years, and due to financial necessity, the petitioner sold the aforesaid plot to Smt. Geeta Rathore, wife of Shri Vidyaram Rathore, resident of Gol Pahadiya, Tighra Road, Madhav Nagar, Gird, Gwalior, for a sum of 28,69,500 on 12/11/2021, by executing a registered sale deed before the Registrar, Gwalior.
Therefore, the applicant rio longer has any possession, control, or authority over the said plot.
5. That at the time when the applicant purchased the said plot, Prashant Jain, the son of Rajendra Jain, was fully aware of the transaction and raised no objection whatsoever at that time.

However,
after the death of his father Shri Rajendra Jain on 17/09/2020, Prashant Jain falsely lodged a First Information Report against the petitioner at Police Station Huzrat Kotwali.
During the lifetime of Rajendra Jain, his son Prashant lain never raised any objection regarding the said transaction.
Nearly two years after the death of Rajendra lain, the said false report has been lodged with the malicious intention of harassing and blackmailing the petitioner.

6. That there existed prior acquaintance and financial disputes between Hemant Pal and the complainant Prashant lain, and due to such monetary disputes between them, the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present matter.

Furthermore, the Station House Officer of Police Station Huzrat Kotwali has also registered the said FIR without conducting any proper inquiry or verifying authentic documentary evidence, apparently with the intention of conferring undue benefit upon the complainant's side, which raises serious questions regarding the conduct and functioning of the said police authority.

7. That in this regard, the petitioner had also submitted a written representation dated 26/03/2022 to the Superintendent of Police and other senior police officials requesting a fair and impartial investigation and seeking to be exonerated from the present case, however, no action has been taken on the said application till date 8.

That, prima facie, no offence is made out against the petitioner in the present matter,
nevertheless, the police have falsely named and implicated the applicant in the said case.
9. That the remaining submissions and arguments shall be presented orally at the time of hearing.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the petition and submitted that the present petition under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No. 62/2022 registered at Police Station NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 5 MCRC-16712-2022 Kotwali, District Gwalior, is liable to be dismissed as the allegations contained in the FIR, taken at their face value, clearly disclose the commission of cognizable offences under Sections 420, 467, and 468 of the IPC.

sentences.text: The material collected during investigation prima facie indicates that the petitioner derived benefit from the alleged forged document and subsequently transferred the property to a third party, thereby forming part of the chain of transactions arising out of the alleged fraud.

At this stage, the defence raised by the petitioner regarding bona fide purchase, prior knowledge of the complainant, or civil nature of the dispute involves disputed questions of fact which cannot be adjudicated in proceedings under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

It is a settled principle that the inherent powers of the High Court are to be exercised sparingly and only in cases where the FIR does not disclose any offence or where continuation of proceedings amounts to abuse of process of law.
Since the allegations in the present case disclose a prima facie case and require proper investigation and trial, the petition for quashment deserves to be rejected.

5. Heard counsel for the State and perused the record.
6.
The scope and ambit of powers of the High Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. are well settled.
The i n h e r e n t j u r i s d i c t i o n o f t h i s C o u r t i s i n t e n d e d t o N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 6 MCRC-16712-2022 prevent abuse of the process of the Court or to secure the ends of justice.
However, such power is to be exercised sparingly, carefully and with great caution.

At the same time, it is equally settled that where the allegations contained in the FIR, even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not constitute any offence against the accused, or where the criminal proceedings are manifestly attended with mala fide intention or instituted with an ulterior motive, the High Court would be justified in exercising its inherent powers to quash such proceedings.
7.

In the present case, the prosecution story, as reflected from the impugned FIR, primarily alleges that the complainant's father had executed a general power of attorney in favour of co-accused Hemant Pal and that the said Hemant Pal, by allegedly misleading the complainant's father,
fraudulently prepared a forged general power of attorney relating to a larger portion of land than what actually remained in the ownership of the complainant's father.
On the basis of the said document, Hemant Pal executed a registered sale deed dated 13.08.2013 in favour of the present petitioner.

8. A careful reading of the allegations contained in the FIR reveals that the principal accusation regarding the alleged act of deceit, fabrication and preparation of the alleged forged document is directed against the co-accused Hemant Pal.
The role attributed to the present petitioner is confined only to the fact that he purchased a portion of land through a registered sale deed executed by the said power of attorney holder.

9. It is noteworthy that the petitioner purchased the property through a NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 7 MCRC-16712-2022 registered sale deed dated 13.08.2013 after the power of attorney had already been executed and registered before the competent authority.

The FIR itself does not disclose any specific allegation that the petitioner had participated in the preparation of the alleged forged power of attorney or that he had any prior knowledge regarding the alleged misrepresentation said to have been made by Hemant Pal while obtaining signatures of the Bharat Baghel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73539724/
4 complainant's father.

sentences.text: The absence of any such specific allegation assumes significance, particularly when the petitioner is merely a purchaser in a transaction executed through a registered instrument.

10. The material placed on record further indicates that the petitioner continued to remain the recorded owner of the said property for a considerable period of time and his name was also mutated in the records of the Municipal Corporation in the year 2019.

It is also not in dispute that during the lifetime of Rajendra Kumar Jain, the alleged executant of the power of attorney, no objection or complaint was raised with regard to the sale deed executed in favour of the petitioner.
The present FIR has been lodged only after the demise of Rajendra Kumar Jain in the year 2020 and nearly nine years after the execution of the sale deed in favour of the petitioner.

11. Such a substantial and unexplained delay in initiating criminal proceedings, coupled with the absence of any allegation demonstrating the petitioner's involvement in the alleged act of forgery,
considerably weakens the substratum of the prosecution case against the petitioner.

In criminal law,
the essential ingredients of the offences under Sections 420, 467 and 468 IPC NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 8 MCRC-16712-2022 include dishonest or fraudulent intention and participation in the act of forgery or cheating.
From the plain reading of the FIR, no such intention or participation on the part of the petitioner can be inferred.
12. At best, the allegations in the FIR disclose a dispute concerning the validity of the power of attorney and the subsequent transactions arising therefrom.
Such a dispute essentially relates to title and validity of documents pertaining to immovable property, which predominantly falls within the realm of civil law.
It is well settled that criminal proceedings should not be permitted to be used as an instrument for settling civil disputes or exerting pressure in matters involving property transactions.

13. It is also a settled principle that where the role attributed to an accused is vague, general and unsupported by specific allegations demonstrating the necessary ingredients of the alleged offences,
the continuation of criminal proceedings would amount to an abuse of the process of law.

In the present case, except for the fact that the petitioner purchased the property through a registered sale deed executed by the power of attorney holder, there is no material indicating that he had any knowledge regarding the alleged forgery or that he acted in conspiracy with the co- accused.
14. Therefore, even if the entire contents of the FIR are accepted as true in their entirety, they do not disclose the commission of the alleged offences by the present petitioner.
Permitting the criminal proceedings to continue against the petitioner in such circumstances would result in unnecessary harassment and misuse of the criminal justice process.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 9 MCRC-16712-2022 15.

Consequently, this Court is of the considered opinion that the case falls within the category of cases where interference under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is warranted in order to secure the ends of justice and to prevent abuse of the process of the Court.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the present petition is allowed.

The FIR bearing Crime No. 62/2022 registered at Police Station Kotwali, District Gwalior for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467 and 468 of the Indian Penal Code and all consequential criminal proceedings arising therefrom, insofar as they relate to the present petitioner Bharat Baghel, stand quashed.
17. The petition stands disposed of accordingly.
